s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertion, associated with ischemic changes on cardiac testing
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Substernal chest pain lasting less than 5 minutes
Chest pain occurs with running more than 2 miles
Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
No chest pain during exercise treadmill test
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

shortlist.label: coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: patient has chest pain with exertion, ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test, and severe ischemia on PET-MPI

shortlist.label: myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: patient has severe ischemia on PET-MPI and 3-vessel involvement on CCTA, indicating high risk for myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: patient has chest pain with exertion, ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test, and severe ischemia on PET-MPI, consistent with acute coronary syndrome

shortlist.label: myocardial ischemia
shortlist.why_kept: patient has severe ischemia on PET-MPI and ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test, indicating myocardial ischemia

shortlist.label: coronary atherosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has 3-vessel involvement on CCTA, indicating coronary atherosclerosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of substernal chest pain with exertion, high LDL, and lack of other explanatory conditions, combined with diagnostic findings of ST depressions during the recovery phase of the exercise treadmill test, 3-vessel involvement on CCTA, severe ischemia on PET-MPI, and confirmation by coronary angiogram, best support a diagnosis of coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: myocardial infarction
rejected.why: There is no evidence of necrosis or damage to heart muscle as would be expected in myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are chronic and occur with exertion, not acute as seen in acute coronary syndrome.

rejected.label: myocardial ischemia
rejected.why: While the patient does have ischemia, this is a symptom rather than a diagnosis, and coronary artery disease is the underlying cause.

rejected.label: coronary atherosclerosis
rejected.why: Coronary atherosclerosis is a component of coronary artery disease but does not fully capture the clinical presentation and diagnostic findings in this case.
